reverse_timeline.event: JANUS TACHYON GATE synthesis from the February lineage
reverse_timeline.core_conclusion: The strongest surviving idea is an adversarial curriculum in which the Keymaker makes the environment harder whenever JANUS improves, while a reverse resource schedule simultaneously gives the agent less compute.

formalization.tachyon_metric_candidate: tau = (DeltaQ * DeltaC) / (-DeltaR), with DeltaQ>0, DeltaC>0, DeltaR<0

architecture: Proof Gate for independently verifiable answers
assistant_preserved_points: The old 'родиться Тахионом' phrase can be retained as a project label, but operationally means improving while the task gets harder and resources shrink.
The Keymaker is interpretable as automatic/adversarial curriculum generation.
The three-node architecture already existed in February: Titan + Android + Beacon feeding a common memory.
Atomic JANUS should use radioactive-decay mathematics as a procedural environment generator rather than claim literal nuclear processing.
A decay environment can use N(t)=N0*exp(-lambda*t) and T_half=ln(2)/lambda, with states disappearing stochastically while the agent solves tasks.
Physarum is useful as a network-contraction metaphor/algorithm: expensive branches die as resources contract, leaving minimal robust paths.
Beacon hashes should authenticate records, not replace raw telemetry for learning.
Correct sensor record architecture is RAW telemetry + timestamp + hash.
Morse should be tested as a preregistered temporal-symbol decoder, not assumed to be spontaneous communication.
Prime numbers can serve as procedural world seeds/modular periods without implying nuclear or mystical privilege.

reverse_timeline.core_conclusion: The usable engineering idea is not that colder clocks literally run faster or that speed crosses zero into negative infinity. It is to select algorithms by progressively removing compute resources and keeping configurations whose quality degrades least.

formalization.reverse_resource_search: theta* = argmax_theta min_(r in R) Q(theta, r)

assistant_preserved_points: Lower semiconductor temperature can reduce leakage and sometimes improve electrical margin, but does not imply that every computation becomes faster as temperature decreases.
Deliberately lowering clock usually increases wall-clock time; the value of throttling here is as selection pressure on the algorithm.
Fahrenheit does not create extra sensor information; F=1.8C+32 is only a unit conversion.
Hardware faults should not be intentionally treated as a normal mutation source; instability can instead define a robustness boundary.
SAT/P-vs-NP experiments must separate heuristic discovery from proof: even excellent scaling on tested instances does not prove P=NP.
If a candidate polynomial algorithm emerges, extract it from the metaheuristic and prove a bound T(n)<=n^k independently.

reverse_timeline.core_conclusion: A full PT transformation reverses both spatial and temporal axes and does not by itself move a hypothetical tachyon from 'ahead of' a photon to 'behind' it in the invariant sense proposed. The physically meaningful discriminator is spacelike separation and Lorentz-frame reversal of temporal ordering.

formalization.spacelike_interval: Delta s^2 = c^2 Delta t^2 - Delta x^2 < 0
formalization.lorentz_time_transform: Delta t' = gamma*(Delta t - u*Delta x/c^2)

assistant_preserved_points: If v>c and two events are spacelike separated, there exist subluminal inertial frames in which their temporal order reverses.
This frame dependence is a mathematical property of spacelike intervals, not evidence that tachyons exist.
A real search would need independently timestamped events, calibrated distance, uncertainty control, and a demonstrated spacelike interval.
Feynman-Stueckelberg antiparticle language should not be confused with literal experimental observation of an electron physically travelling backward through macroscopic time.

reverse_timeline.event: Thermal-Aware Evolutionary AI / digital homeostasis concept
historical_claims_and_design: Temperature was proposed as a truth/stability filter rather than only a hardware limit.
Three Physarum modes were proposed: HOT/EXPLORE, FREEZE, CONTRACT.
Revertive Search stores a best stable state and rolls back when quality drops or temperature rises.
A regulation example used approximately 70C/158F as a high-temperature threshold and approximately 50C/122F as a cool zone.
The system was proposed to learn from real hardware metrics and execution variability.
Hardware Entropy was proposed as the variance of repeated-operation execution time.
The system should adapt to actual hardware instead of assuming one fixed GPU/CPU environment.
historical_hardware_noise_claims: The old dialogue suggested using soft errors, cache errors, bus timing, ECC errors, clock jitter and voltage droop as mutation/selection signals.

Current correction: normal operation at common high temperatures does not imply frequent random bit flips; instability must be measured and treated as a robustness boundary, not presumed beneficial noise.
